messages:
maya: Nightly multi-GPU smoke is red on shard 7. Failing during allreduce with long stalls and nvlink errors in dmesg. Can someone eyeball?
ci-bot: Job: https://ci.redwood.internal/ops/12345 (commit a7b9c2f) triggered nightly at 2026-03-17T02:15Z :robot_face:
maya: Quick paste of the relevant bits from the node where it failed: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, pid=9876, 0x00000000, 0x00000000
[ 1234.568000] nvlink: link 2 error: bandwidth drop detected
[ 1234.568100] nvlink: resetting link 2
[ 1234.580000] allreduce: epoch wait > 120s, barrier stuck
```
and nvidia-smi nvlink --status returned multiple "Port 2: Link down" lines.
devon: Ugh. Can you grab the node PCI topology and dmesg full tail + the tester container logs? quick commands: 
```
kubectl logs -n ci job/gpu-smoke-2471234567 -c tester --tail=200
ssh node-7 'dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i nvlink'
ssh node-7 'nvidia-smi nvlink --status'
```
maya: Pasted logs above are the dmesg tail. tester logs show repeated NCCL timeouts: "unhandled exception: allreduce timed out after 120s" and then retries.
raja: Two quick hypotheses: 1) NVLink lane degraded on that chassis (hardware), 2) driver/firmware mismatch after last image rollout (we bumped kernel and switched CUDA toolkit). Did that node get the new runtime image?
ingrid: Also possible PCIe bifurcation/slot reseat during maintenance. Which rack is node-7 in? if it's the single-rack switch, others in same rack also flaked earlier this week.
maya: node-7 is dgx-3.rackB. I reran the same job pinned to dgx-3 and it failed. Reran the job on dgx-12.rackC and it passed green. So looks node-local. :eyes:
devon: Good repro. That points towards hardware/firmware. Can infra try a quick nvlink bringup and firmware query? commands: 
```
ssh dgx-3 'nvidia-smi -q | egrep -i "Firmware Version|Bridge"'
ssh dgx-3 'nvlink-topology -v || nvidia-smi nvlink --status'
```
raja: If infra confirms NVSwitch firmware drift, we should exclude dgx-3 from nightly pool until fixed. Also file a bisect of the node image to ensure not a subtle driver regression (but hardware seems likely since other racks fine).
ci-bot: Note: recent infra rollout 2026-03-16 23:40Z updated node images for rackB (kernel 6.4.2 + CUDA 12.2 runtime).
maya: That matches timing. However, dgx-12 was updated too and passed. Could be a partial firmware mismatch on dgx-3. Will request infra to check nvlink PHY logs and reseat the NVSwitch interconnect.
ingrid: Short-term mitigation: add a pre-smoke nvlink-health check that runs on all nodes and fails fast, so we can auto-exclude bad nodes. Suggest a tiny NCCL-rw test or `nvidia-smi nvlink --status` parse.
devon: Agree. Put it in the pod init container so CI fails quicker and doesn't waste hours. Also label nodes with nvlink-healthy=true/false via cluster-api for routing.
maya: I'll open a ticket to infra with logs and request a hardware check on dgx-3 (nvlink ports 2/3 reported down). I'll also add a tiny precheck to the smoke job.
raja: If infra flags firmware mismatch: plan is to rollback kernel/CUDA image on that node and re-run smoke; if it repros after rollback then escalate to hardware replacement.
maya: Action items I will do: 1) file infra ticket + attach dmesg + nvlink status (I'll include the `nvidia-smi` dumps), 2) add init-container precheck PR to smoke job (short script), 3) re-run nightly with dgx-3 excluded until fixed.
maya: Quick note — here's the init check I'm planning to add: 
```
#!/bin/bash
# fail fast if nvlink ports report down
nvidia-smi nvlink --status | grep -i "Link.*down" && exit 1 || exit 0
```
devon: LGTM. small nit: make it tolerant for older drivers that don't support nvlink command (fallback to a 1-GPU skip).
ci-bot: Created ticket INFRA-8943 and pinned job rerun: https://ci.redwood.internal/ops/12346 (rerun excluding dgx-3)
maya: Rerun excluding dgx-3 succeeded. Marking CI green for now and leaving the infra ticket. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
raja: :thumbsup: please update the nightly run doc with the auto-exclude rule once PR is merged.
maya: Will do. Closing out here after infra confirms hardware/firmware root cause.
